headline: Elected Kate Doyle as Vice-Chair and adopted Vision 2026 Nine Point Agenda as focus for the year
summary: The Commission approved November 2025 and January 2026 meeting minutes with corrections. Members received updates on Blue Envelope legislation, the Lions Club collaboration, the All Abilities Bird Walk, the MOD Grant, and the Fells Feasibility Study. The Commission elected Kate Doyle as Vice-Chair and adopted the Vision 2026 Nine Point Agenda, assigning members to specific focus areas.
decisions: Approved the November 2025 minutes with a correction to Amanda Belles' name
Approved the January 2026 minutes with a correction
Adopted Vision 2026 as the Commission's focus for the year

1 | Page  
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
Disability Commission Meeting Minutes 
February 12, 2026 
Attendance: 
 
 
Members of the Disability Commission participated in the meeting remotely per the 
Governor’s legislation of March 28, 2025, suspending certain provisions of the open meeting 
law. A Microsoft Teams link was also provided for members of the public who wished to 
attend 
 
This meeting was also recorded through Microsoft Teams and called to order at 6:08PM. 
 
1.  Roll call of Committee Members 
Chuks started the meeting and mentioned that it would be recorded via Microsoft 
Teams. He then called attendance as indicated in the chart above and a quorum was 
present to conduct business. Each member gave a self-description when responding 
to roll call.   
 
2. Approval of Meeting Minutes 
The November 2025 Meeting Minutes which were tabled from the last meeting were 
discussed. It was pointed out that Amanda Belles’ name was misspelled. Upon 
motion of Amanda to approve the November 2025 minutes with the correction, 
seconded by Kate D., the Commission voted unanimously by roll call vote to approve 
the minutes.   
 
The January 2026 minutes were also discussed. Kate D. mentioned that she was not 
at that meeting in person. Upon motion of Marilyn to approve the January 2026 
minutes with the correction, seconded by Ralph, the Commission voted unanimously 
by roll call vote to approve the minutes.     
 
 
3. Updates or Action Items that need to be Addressed from Previous Meetings

• Blue Envelope Legislation: Maria reported that on behalf of the City and the 
Commission, Mayor Christenson sent a letter supporting the Blue Envelope 
legislation to the State Representatives. Receipt was acknowledged.  
• Lions Club Collaboration: Chuks was in the process of connecting with Michelle 
Luong and attending a Lions Club meeting.  
• All Abilities Bird Walk: Kate D. updated the Commission on the upcoming spring 
all-abilities bird walk and resource fair, noting that for now there was no official 
date. The event may be postponed to July to coincide with Disability Pride Month 
and is expected to be larger than last year, with pre-event activities to build 
excitement. 
• MOD Grant: Maria updated the Commission on the Mass Office of Disability 
grant. She is working with Eric Rubin to obtain quotes to upgrade high school 
bathrooms with accessible sinks. She will keep everyone updated. 
• Fells Feasibility Study: Maria reported that the Friends of the Fells had reached 
out because they are applying for a grant in order to conduct a Feasibility Study 
on adding an accessible trail in the Fells. If they receive the grant they will reach 
back out for the Commission’s input on the project.  
5.   New Business 
• Marilyn and Chuks reported on the opening of the new Tufts Medicine Behavioral 
Health Hospital on the old Malden Hospital site. They both attended the grand 
opening along with Kate D. and Lisa. Marilyn explained that this is a 144-bed, 
facility offering inpatient and intensive outpatient care for children, adolescents, 
adults, and seniors. It will focus on mental health and substance use disorders. 
• Election of the Vice Chair: Marilyn nominated Kate Doyle for vice chair, citing her 
enthusiasm and contributions. Kate expressed interest and accepted the 
nomination. Upon motion of Marilyn to elect Kate Doyle as Vice-Chair, seconded 
by Ralph, the Commission voted unanimously by roll call vote to elect Kate D. 
• Chuks introduced the Vision 2026: Nine Point Agenda and he explained that this 
was a way for Commission members to take responsibility for specific areas of 
accessibility and inclusivity, with assignments made and expectations set for 
progress reports at meetings. 
 
He explained the T I E S H E R R A Framework and used this acronym to organize 
eﬀorts across Transportation, Infrastructure, Education, Social Activities, Health, 
Employment, Recreation, Religion, Rehabilitation, and Accommodation. The goal 
is to make an impact in each of these sectors. Members volunteered for the area 
they were most interested in. The assignments are as follows: 
   
Member Assignments:  
Transportation and Infrastructure: Lisa noted that she was already working on 
this area with the Mayor. 
Education: Marilyn 
Social Activities and Health: Kate D. 
Employment Activities: Maria
3 | Page  
 
Religion: Ralph 
Housing: Chuks 
Kate H. and Shanti can also assist in the areas of their choosing. 
For the March meeting, Chuks asked that each member report on any progress in 
their assigned sector. This will help to make recommendations to the Mayor. 
After further discussion, upon motion of Ralph to accept Vision 2026 as the 
Commission's focus for the year, seconded by Maria, the Commission voted 
unanimously to adopt Visions 2026 by roll call vote. 
6. Public Comment 
No one spoke for public comment.  
 
7.   Scheduling of next meeting and adjournment 
The next meeting was scheduled for Thursday, March 12, 2026 at 6:00PM.  
 
Upon the motion of Maria to adjourn, which was seconded by Marilyn, the Commission 
voted unanimously to adjourn the meeting.
